question: What is the main goal of diet therapy in patient care?

options.A: Modifying regular food intake to meet specific health needs
options.C: Ensuring every patient eats the exact same meal
options.D: Replacing all forms of medical drug treatment

explanation: You've got this! Diet therapy is simply tailoring a patient's nutrition to help them heal, manage an illness, or balance their body's needs. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why is diet therapy such an important part of your daily nursing duties?

options.A: Nurses must personally cook all meals served in the hospital ward
options.B: Nurses are responsible for monitoring patient tolerance and supporting the prescribed nutrition plan
options.C: Dietary plans replace the need for physical assessments
options.D: Doctors never check what patients are eating

explanation: Since you spend the most time with patients, you are in the best position to see if they are enjoying their food and how well their body is handling it! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h1)

question: When you measure a patient's mid-upper arm circumference and body mass index, what kind of assessment are you doing?
explanation: Don't let the big word scare you! 'Anthropometric' just means measuring physical body sizes like height, weight, and arm circumference to check nutrition. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h2)

question: You check a patient's lab results, like serum albumin and electrolytes. What type of nutritional data is this?
explanation: Spot on! Lab tests and blood markers give you biochemical data, showing what is happening inside the patient's body chemically. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h2)

question: A patient just had jaw surgery and cannot chew solid foods. Which diet type is best for them?
explanation: Easy choice! Soft and mechanical diets change the texture of food so it's super easy to chew and swallow when the mouth or jaw needs a break. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is a major risk if a recovering patient stays on a clear liquid diet for too long?

options.A: It triggers sudden weight gain from excess fats
options.B: It causes severe high blood pressure
options.C: It permanently ruins the patient's sense of taste
options.D: It can lead to hospital-derived malnutrition due to very low calorie and nutrient content

explanation: Clear liquids are great at first, but they don't have enough energy and nutrients. Keeping patients on them too long starves their healing body! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h3)

question: What is the main dietary focus when caring for a patient with high blood pressure (hypertension)?
explanation: You know this! Cutting down on salt (sodium) helps reduce fluid retention and lowers pressure inside the blood vessels. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h4)

question: A patient with type 2 diabetes asks why they need to eat more fiber. How should you explain it?

options.A: Fiber slows down digestion, which helps prevent sharp blood sugar spikes after meals
options.B: Fiber increases blood sugar levels rapidly for quick energy
options.C: Fiber completely cures diabetes within a few days of eating it
options.D: Fiber replaces the need to ever take diabetes medication again

explanation: Great nursing communication! Fiber slows down how fast sugar enters the blood, keeping those glucose levels nice and steady after eating. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h4)

question: In community health nursing, what are Ready-to-Use Therapeutic Foods (RUTF) mainly used for?

options.B: Treating high blood pressure in adults
options.C: Treating severe acute malnutrition safely at home

explanation: RUTFs are nutrient-packed pastes that save lives by helping severely malnourished children recover right at home without needing a hospital bed. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h5)

question: Why do primary health care nurses encourage families to use local foods like beans and groundnuts for children?

options.A: They contain zero calories and prevent childhood obesity
options.B: They provide affordable, accessible plant proteins and nutrients for growing children
options.C: They completely cure infectious diseases like malaria
options.D: They are the only foods that do not require cooking

explanation: Using cheap, locally available foods makes good nutrition practical and sustainable for everyday families in our communities. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h5)

question: Why is it so helpful to involve family members when giving diet counseling to a patient?

options.A: It prevents the patient from ever eating outside the home
options.B: Family members pay all the hospital medical bills
options.C: Family members usually prepare the household meals and manage food purchases
options.D: Family members are legally required to taste all hospital food first

explanation: Since family members are usually the ones cooking at home, bringing them into the conversation ensures the new diet is actually doable for the household! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h6)

question: A patient complains that their prescribed diet cuts out all their favorite cultural dishes and feels impossible. What is your best response?

options.A: Tell the patient they have no choice and must strictly obey the prescription
options.B: Work with the patient to find healthy substitutes and modify their favorite cultural meals
options.C: Ignore the complaint since food preferences do not affect health outcomes
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating entirely until they adjust to the new menu

explanation: That's patient-centered care! Respecting their culture and tweaking their favorite meals makes it much more likely they will stick to the plan. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h6)

question: How can you tell over time if a patient's diet therapy is working successfully?

options.B: The brand of cutlery used for meals
options.C: The exact time the hospital kitchen opens
options.D: The color of the hospital room walls

explanation: Checking changes in body weight and lab results gives you clear, undeniable proof of how well the therapeutic diet is working. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h7)

question: What should you suspect first if a patient's lab results don't improve even though they claim to follow their diet?

options.A: The dietary plan, adherence, or overall treatment approach needs re-evaluation
options.B: The patient must be hiding food inside their mattress
options.C: The patient has been cured of the disease completely
options.D: Laboratory tests are never accurate in clinical practice

explanation: When numbers don't budge, it's a cue for the healthcare team to pause, check if the diet is truly working, and make adjustments together. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h7)
